strategy.summary: Reproduce the blur_effect NaN on constant images at the buggy commit bb7f08a4c802 by installing that revision in editable mode with a numpy<2 environment, then run the two new tests from the PR. On the buggy revision the constant-image assertions fail because 0/0 yields NaN; on the fixed revision the epsilon floor on the denominator should make them return exactly 1.

pinned_because: numpy<2: no documented constraint exists; this pin is era-inferred from the 2022-2023 timeframe of the PR, which predates numpy 2.0, and is chosen by this strategy rather than stated in the evidence
python 3.10: era-inferred choice for a 2023-era scikit-image dev build; not documented in the evidence
build deps (Cython, meson-python) are needed for the compiled skimage extensions at this revision; inferred from the build system, not stated in the evidence
scikit-image: unpinned in the sense that the revision under test is the checkout itself, so no PyPI version is selected

strategy.reproducing_test: test_blur_effect_uniform_input (parametrized factor in 0, 1, 2.5) and test_blur_single_axis_constant_image (parametrized shape in (10, 11), (4, 5, 6)) in skimage/measure/tests/test_blur_effect.py
strategy.success_criterion: Transition: on the buggy revision bb7f08a4c802 the uniform-input tests fail (blur_effect returns NaN, so assert B == 1 is False; a RuntimeWarning about invalid value in scalar divide is emitted), and on the fixed revision the same tests pass with B == 1 exactly. The single-axis test is expected to fail on buggy only if the NaN path is reached; otherwise it is a regression guard that passes on both.
strategy.numerical_probe: ski.measure.blur_effect(np.zeros((10,10,3)), channel_axis=-1) should be finite and equal to 1 on the fixed revision, and NaN on the buggy one.

input_output_examples.buggy_output: RuntimeWarning: invalid value encountered in scalar divide; returns np.nan

risks: _EPSILON value is not stated in the evidence; it is only described as a multiple of spacing, so the fixed-revision result depends on code not visible here
Exact equality B == 1 in the tests means that any floating-point rounding on the fixed revision would fail the test; the transition assumes the fixed code yields exactly 1.0
The issue example uses dtype=int while the new tests use float; the evidence does not say the defect depends on dtype, so both are assumed to trigger it

The single-axis test (row broadcast along axis 0) may not produce 0/0 on the buggy revision, because the denominator for the non-uniform axis is nonzero; it may therefore pass on buggy and not form part of the transition
Issue discussion proposed raising ValueError instead of returning 1.0; if the fixed revision raises rather than returns, the test transition would be different and this strategy would not match
The test diff also rewrites existing tests to use the ski alias; applying the whole test file from the fix is required, and the other tests may behave differently on the buggy revision
Building the compiled extensions requires a working C/C++ toolchain; if the build fails, the buggy revision cannot be exercised at all
No platform or architecture dependency is stated in the evidence, so no arch- or sanitizer-specific behaviour is assumed; the defect is expected to be platform-independent

oracle.reference_source: PR #7643 body: constant images should return 1.0
oracle.why: The test asserts B == 1 exactly, and the PR states that a constant image is perfectly blurred, so the expected value is exactly 1.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: On bb7f08a4c802 blur_effect divides by M1 which is 0 for any constant image (gradient of a constant is zero regardless of value), giving 0/0 = NaN with a RuntimeWarning; assert B == 1 sees NaN, and NaN == 1 is False, so the assertion fails.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: On the fixed revision the denominator is floored by _EPSILON via np.maximum, so the ratio is finite and the metric evaluates to 1 for uniform inputs, so assert B == 1 holds.
